title: lava list --json
description: Every command this app can run, grouped by the pack that provides it. The command set is a boot decision — a pack that is enabled contributes commands — so the app is booted to answer it, but a failed boot is NOT an error here: 'what can I still run?' is the question most worth answering when the app is broken. `booted` records that the answer may be missing pack commands, and diagnosing why is `lava check`'s job.

commands.description: In registration order: core first (orient, verify, the tables, the runner, the lookup), then each pack's.

name.description: What to type. Names are unique across core, packs, and the app — a duplicate is a fatal boot problem, never a silent override.

flags.description: Flag names without their leading dashes; `json` is always among them.

pack.description: The pack providing it, by its short name — `core`, or the pack's feature name (`db` for `lavaphp/db`, whose commands are the `db:*` ones). The package name is what `app/Modules.php` and `composer require` use; this is the name the pack calls itself.

schema.description: The contract name this command's envelope claims — `lava.routes/1`, or `lava.db.status/1` for a pack command, whose colon cannot survive into a file name. The contract is the file `docs/schemas/<schema>.json`. Versioned per command, so this is the field that tells a caller which shape to expect rather than which to assume.

booted.description: False when the app failed to boot: the list is then the core set only, and pack commands are unknown rather than absent.
